title: Partisan and platform boundary of the video effects
why: Addresses the missing moderator and sample causes: the one nominal Republican interaction (Message 15, +0.165, p = 0.004) was found across 32 tests and needs a targeted confirmatory test.

power_target.basis: Observed Message 15 by Republican interaction of 0.165 (SE 0.057); interaction contrasts need about 4 times the main-effect n, sized to an MDE near 0.1.

rationale: In the source study, Messages 15 and 20 raised trust by about 0.06 points (p = 0.012 for Message 15), but the one nominal Republican interaction (Message 15, +0.165, SE 0.057, p = 0.004) came from 32 uncorrected tests. All exposure was forced, so it is unknown whether the effects hold in a feed. This design tests the interaction directly and crosses it with exposure setting.
contribution: Gives a confirmatory test of whether two small positive video effects on trust in science differ by Republican identification and by forced versus feed exposure.
hypothesis: Message 15 raises trust more among Republicans than non-Republicans (interaction about +0.165). Effects are smaller in the feed than under forced exposure.
primary_outcome: Trust in science: mean of 6 items, with items 4-6 reverse-coded (post_science_1 to post_science_6).
comparison: Message 15 and Message 20 versus control, moderated by Republican identification (pre-registered) and by exposure setting.
unresolved: The actual Message 15 and 20 video files and the simulated feed must be produced by the research team.
IRB number and compensation to be supplied.
label: Generalizability

title: Replicate the extremes to separate real effects from chance
why: Fixes the multiplicity and power problem: a preregistered confirmatory test of 4 arms replaces 32 exploratory contrasts, so the two positions of the debate are discriminated.

power_target.basis: Observed +0.063 for Messages 15 and 20; the larger Message 2 effect (-0.171) would need only about 550 per arm.

rationale: The source ran 32 uncorrected contrasts; Message 2 lowered trust by 0.171 (p=0.0002) while Messages 15 and 20 raised it by about 0.063 (p<0.05), and only about 2 of 32 hits is what chance would give. A preregistered four-arm replication with Holm correction tests whether these extremes persist.
contribution: Provides a confirmatory, multiplicity-corrected test of whether brief messages can move trust in science, discriminating the position that they can from the position that trust is sticky.
hypothesis: If brief messages can move trust, Messages 15 and 20 will raise post-trust by about +0.06 and Message 2 will lower it by -0.10 or more. If the original hits were chance, all four contrasts will shrink toward zero.
primary_outcome: Post-treatment trust in science: mean of six items, with items 4-6 reverse-coded.
comparison: Each of Messages 2, 15, 20 and 26 versus the fresh control, pre-trust adjusted, Holm-corrected across four tests.
unresolved: Original video files for Messages 2, 15, 20 and 26 must be supplied by the research team.
IRB number and compensation are to be supplied.
The exact source scale item wording must be confirmed.
label: Theoretical debate
